figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Two Amycolatopsis sp. strains isolated from desert soil produce aridomycins A−C. (A) F10 and GA6-03 produce the same major
compounds that elute at 10.7 (1, red) and 12.3 min (2, black). Supernatants from cultures of F10 and GA6-03 grown for 4 days were extracted with
n-butanol and analyzed by HPLC with UV detection at 254 nm. (B,C) Negative mode MS/MS spectra of chromatographed peaks detected at 10.7
min (B, in red, precursor m/z 1354.7353) and 12.3 min (C, in black, precursor m/z 1192.6808). (D) Structures of aridomycin A (1), B (2) and
presumed shunt product C (3).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. NMR structure determination of 1−3. (A) Key 1H−1H COSY and HMBC correlations in aridomycin A−C (1−3) are shown. The
glucose unit is represented as an R group (red). The backbone connectivities were confirmed from a 2D 13C−COSY-45 spectrum recorded on a
10% 13C-labeled sample of 1 (Figure S2). (B−F) NOEs used to establish relative configurations for C1−C15 (B), C19−C22 in 3 (C and D), the E
geometry of the C-43−C-44 olefin (E), and the hexose unit in 1 (F). (G) Stick representation of an energy minimized model of aridomycin C (3)
showing the positions of the polyketide chains on the tetrahydropyran ring. (H−M) Newman projections showing relative configurations and J-
based configurational analysis for C9/C10 and C15 through C20. See Figure S3 for additional rotamers of C18/C19. 1H COSY correlations are
depicted with bold bonds in 2A, and NOEs and 1H−1H coupling constants are shown with double-headed blue and red arrows, respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Relative configurations of regions containing 1,3-diols and 2-methyl-1,3-diols using Kishi’s Universal NMR Databases. (A) Assignment of
2-methyl-1,3-diols using database 4.16 (B) Assignment of 1,3-diols with NMR database 2.17 13C chemical shifts for the stereoisomers within the
databases and experimental values are shown.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Aridomycin biosynthetic gene cluster reveals a new AT domain specificity motif for hydroxymalonyl-ACP. (A) ari gene cluster from
Amycolatopsis sp. F10 and GA6-03. (B) Sequence alignment of ari AT domains showing the extender unit substrate specificity motifs. Catalytic
residues appear in bold and specificity motifs are color coded as follows: V/HAFH motif in yellow for malonyl-CoA; Q/FVAH in green for
hydroxymalonyl-ACP; Q/YASH in light blue for methylmalonyl-CoA. The third AT domain in ariI (AriI_AT3) is missing the catalytic Ser and His
residues and is therefore inactive and not included. Multiple sequence alignment performed with Clustal Omega.19

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Biosynthetic pathway for aridomycin A (1) and aridomycin B (2). The proposed hybrid NRPS-PKS pathway was inferred from the
genome sequences of strains F10 and GA6-03 (respective GenBank accession numbers CP176065.1 and CP176499.1). Individual genes are shown
as thick black arrows. PKS modules are indicated by black bars, numbered consecutively from the loading module through module 22. Distinct PKS
and NRPS domains are represented by circles: filled (black) circles denote catalytically inactive domains, while open circles indicate skipped
domains. Structures of the predicted polyketide intermediates are shown below each module. Module 1 or 2 is proposed to iterate twice to generate
the triene; for illustration, double iteration is shown on module 2. Chemical structures are color-coded according to the incorporated extender unit:

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Activity, substrate specificity and self-immunity function of
the glycosyltransferase AriGT, in the aridomycin BGC. (A) Time
course quantitation of aridomycin B (2) and aridomycin A (1) over 7
days. Supernatants were extracted with n-butanol and analyzed by
reverse phase (RP)-HPLC with UV detection at 254 nm. Experiments
were performed in triplicate; data represent mean ± standard
deviation. (B) Stacked RP-HPLC chromatograms showing standards
of aridomycin B and aridomycin A and representative AriGT
glucosylation reactions. Reactions were carried out with 50 nM
AriGT or 1 μM AriGT-H15A, 100 μM aridomycin, and 500 μM of
the indicated UDP-sugar for 10 min. (C) Substrate specificity of
AriGT toward aridomycin and two macrolide antibiotics, erythromy-
cin and tylosin. Reactions were performed with 1 μM AriGT, 100 μM
acceptor substrate, and 500 μM UDP-Glc. Aridomycin B and tylosin
were quantified by HPLC with UV detection at 254 nm;
erythromycin was quantitated by LC-MS.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Model of Amycolatopsis strains GA6-03 and F10 self-
resistance to aridomycin B. Schematic shows aridomycin B biosyn-
thesis, highlighting the self-protection through glucosylation into
aridomycin A, and release of the active antimicrobial by the glycoside
hydrolase AriGH.
